newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Hawker says Austrim bid opportunistic.
newsitem.headline: Hawker says Austrim bid opportunistic.

text.p: Manufacturing group Hawker Richardson Ltd said on Wednesday the proposed takeover bid by investment group Austim Ltd was opportunistically timed to take advantage of Hawker's growth potential.
"We have got ourselves into growth mode - we think we can take the company forward to new heights without anybody's help," Hawker chief Graeme Salthouse told a news conference.
Hawker earlier rejected Austrim's bid of A$1.60 per share and said the market had indicated that the offer was inadequate.
At 3.45 p.m (0545 GMT) Hawker shares were down nine cents at A$1.71.
But they have traded as high as A$1.81 since the bid was announced on Tuesday.
Salthouse said he did not believe Austrim was targeting cost saving from the potential takeover of Hawker and that Austrim's existing businesses did not have many synergies with Hawker.
"We come from the industrial sector of manufacturing and we have very deliberately taken ourselves into high margin business, highly profitable business," Sathouse said.
Salthouse said he had enormous regard for Austim chairman, Alan Jackson, the former chief executive of BTR Plc, but said Hawker's management could deliver growth to shareholders as well as Jackson.
"We have opportunities out there right now that we are looking at," he said.
Hawker doubled in size last year when it acquired aerospace and precision engineering manufacturer T.E.D. Engineering in November for A$24.3 million.
The purchase was mainly funded by a placemment to institutions which raised A$18.4 million.
Institutions now hold about 70 percent of the company's issued capital.
Earlier this month Hawker floated computer data security company, Secure Network Solutions Ltd, and retained a 19 percent stake in that company.
